record.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt models for multimodal agents and local deployment
record.summary: NVIDIA announced Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and two Bolt open models on Oct. 15; Bolt E4B was released on Oct. 23 for a roughly 4GB target. Its 8B-total/4B-effective checkpoint is based on Gemma 4 E4B-it, with Q4_K_M and BF16 versions, 64K context and configurable reasoning. NVIDIA publishes separate BF16 and Q4_K_M benchmark columns in the model card and hardware-specific serving measurements. Results are vendor-run and mixed: the Q4_K_M model trails Qwen 3.5 4B on several tool-use and long-context rows. No independent reproduction or task-level deployment evaluation was performed.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: NVIDIA announced Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and two Bolt variants on Oct. 15, stating that Bolt E4B was scheduled for Oct. 23.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: NVIDIA describes Super VL as a 120B multimodal model, Bolt 74B-A9B as a model for 24GB deployment, and Bolt E4B as a small model targeting roughly 4GB deployment.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: NVIDIA reports up to 5x faster task completion/throughput for Super VL versus its comparison class; this review did not independently assess the comparison.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: NVIDIA lists Bolt E4B as released Oct. 23, 2026 and reports separate BF16 and Q4_K_M benchmark results plus hardware-specific latency, memory and throughput measurements. Results are mixed across named tasks; this review did not independently reproduce them.

evidence_gaps.description: Independent evaluations under matched quality, memory, throughput and task-completion conditions are absent, including for the newly released Bolt E4B checkpoint.
The linked E4B training recipe and evaluation artifacts were not retrieved or audited; benchmark prompt sets and full configuration details remain unverified.

brief.importance_rationale: If the stated capabilities and deployment tradeoffs hold, a 120B multimodal agent model plus variants targeting 24GB and 4GB devices could expand where open-weight agent systems can run and be adapted. This is consequential for inference access and evaluation, but announced performance and adoption remain vendor claims without independent measurement in this review.
limitations: All model and benchmark claims come from NVIDIA; no independent reproduction, matched external evaluation or application-level deployment test was performed.

The research page's detailed benchmark table is labeled BF16; the linked Hugging Face model card separately provides BF16 and Q4_K_M columns across 20 benchmark rows. These provider-run results are mixed: Q4_K_M Bolt E4B trails Qwen 3.5 4B on several tool-use and long-context rows, including BFCL-v3, Tau2-Bench, RULER and LongBench v2.

NVIDIA states that the benchmark harness is consistent across models but reasoning mode varies by benchmark. The report says Brevity Bench and When2Call-MT address evaluation gaps and were not yet released; leaderboard results do not establish better behavior in target applications.
The claimed up-to-80% output-token reduction is a provider comparison and does not by itself establish equal task quality, lower end-to-end latency or lower total inference cost.

Serving figures are specific to NVIDIA's named hardware, llama.cpp/CUDA and AIPerf setup, batch size one, quantization and input/output lengths; performance can differ with software, hardware and configuration.
Partner customization and integration examples are reported by NVIDIA and do not establish adoption scale or outcomes.
This development combines the Oct. 15 model-family announcement with the Oct. 23 E4B release; event dates remain separate within the source records.
brief.summary: NVIDIA announced Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and two Bolt open models on Oct. 15; Bolt E4B was released on Oct. 23 for a roughly 4GB target. Its 8B-total/4B-effective checkpoint is based on Gemma 4 E4B-it, with Q4_K_M and BF16 versions, 64K context and configurable reasoning. NVIDIA publishes separate BF16 and Q4_K_M benchmark columns in the model card and hardware-specific serving measurements. Results are vendor-run and mixed: the Q4_K_M model trails Qwen 3.5 4B on several tool-use and long-context rows. No independent reproduction or task-level deployment evaluation was performed.

technical.claimed_result: NVIDIA reports average quality gains versus its prior Nano 4B model and selected peers, plus up to 80% fewer output tokens in some reasoning-enabled comparisons. Its model card provides separate BF16 and Q4_K_M results across 20 benchmark rows. In Q4_K_M comparisons, the model scores higher on some rows and lower than Qwen 3.5 4B on others, including BFCL-v3, Tau2-Bench, LongMemEval, LongBench v2 and RULER. These are NVIDIA-run NeMo Gym evaluations; no independent reproduction was done.
technical.compute_or_cost: Training cost is not reported. NVIDIA provides Q4_K_M single-session serving measurements: on RTX 5070 at 3K input/50 output tokens it reports 3.5 GB VRAM, 548 ms time to first token and 133.4 tokens/s; at 32K cached context plus 2K input/256 output it reports 4.3 GB, 1,238 ms and 106.2 tokens/s. These are vendor-run, hardware/software-specific measurements, not independent costs or general deployment guarantees.
technical.demonstrated_result: NVIDIA's Oct. 23 research page and Hugging Face model card expose the E4B release, report, release date, 8B-total/4B-effective Gemma-4-E4B architecture, Q4_K_M and BF16 variants, 64K context, configurable reasoning, post-training recipe links and separate BF16/Q4_K_M benchmark tables. These establish what NVIDIA published, not the validity of its reported model performance; no independent run was performed.
technical.implementation_status: NVIDIA announced Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B availability on Oct. 15 and scheduled E4B for Oct. 23; the E4B model card lists its release date as Oct. 23, 2026 and names Hugging Face and build.nvidia.com availability.
technical.mechanism: Bolt E4B is post-trained from Gemma-4-E4B-it using NVIDIA's NeMo-RL/NeMo-Gym reinforcement-learning recipe across instruction following, multi-turn tool use, conversation and structured outputs, then quantized to Q4_K_M using llama.cpp and an importance-matrix calibration set. NVIDIA also publishes a DFlash speculative drafter.
technical.novelty: The Oct. 23 release adds a documented small open checkpoint aimed at conversational and multi-turn tool-using agents under a roughly 4GB model-storage target, with a separate BF16 checkpoint and speculative drafter. Novelty here is the release/artifact and stated deployment envelope, not independently established superiority.
technical.regime: The Q4_K_M model has 8B total and 4B effective parameters, text input/output and a stated 64K context. NVIDIA reports batch-size-one tests with llama.cpp/CUDA and AIPerf on RTX 5070, RTX Spark, Jetson Orin Nano and Jetson AGX Orin; the reported memory, time-to-first-token and throughput vary by hardware and sequence lengths.
technical.reproducibility: The model page links checkpoints, training data/recipe material and evaluation methodology. This review inspected the public research page and Hugging Face card but did not download/run weights, retrieve all linked recipe artifacts or independently reproduce benchmark values.
technical.strongest_baseline: NVIDIA's Hugging Face card compares Q4_K_M Bolt E4B with Q4_K_M Gemma 4 E4B-it, Qwen 3.5 4B and Nemotron 3 Nano 4B in a shared NeMo Gym harness. Reported Qwen 3.5 4B scores are higher on BFCL-v3 (70.56 vs 67.31), Tau2-Bench (61.74 vs 52.32), RULER (95.37 vs 85.76), and LongBench v2 (58.28 vs 48.67); Bolt E4B scores higher on other rows, including MultiChallenge and RoleBench. The card says reasoning mode is consistent across models within each benchmark, but varies by benchmark. The results are provider-run and not independently reproduced.

brief.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt models for multimodal agents and local deployment
brief.why_it_matters: A small open model with tool-use post-training and a roughly 4GB deployment target could widen the hardware range for local agents. The Oct. 23 technical report provides an inspectable model card, recipe and NVIDIA-run measurements, but does not establish independent quality, latency or deployment advantages.
